evidence_quote: We decompose the 11D action vector into four functional groups $\mathcal{G} = \{\text{arm}, \text{gripper}, \text{head}, \text{base}\}$ and compute: ... $\text{MSE}_g = \frac{1}{|g|} \sum_{j \in g} (\hat{a}_j - a_j)^2$
statement: The authors evaluate models by decomposing the 11D action vector into four functional groups (arm, gripper, head, base) and computing the mean squared error for each group.

evidence_quote: Phase 1: pretraining on a 109,269-episode subset (531 tasks) of the ICRA 2026 workshop dataset for 20k steps... Phase 2: task-specific fine-tuning on a six-task pick-up release from the same workshop (3,971 episodes)
statement: SmolVLA was pretrained on a 109,269-episode subset of the ICRA 2026 workshop dataset and fine-tuned on a 3,971-episode pick-up task release.

evidence_quote: The base is the last group to converge and sets the ceiling on the aggregate. This is the sense in which the mobile base is the bottleneck of SmolVLA fine-tuning.

evidence_quote: expert-only 3k underperforms the untouched baseline despite having lower total MSE (0.95 vs. 1.04) ... the gains concentrate on the gripper and the base ... while the arm (already well-predicted at 0.30) degrades to 0.59.
statement: Expert-only fine-tuning of the pi_0.5 model reduces total MSE but degrades arm accuracy, resulting in worse real-robot performance compared to the untouched baseline.

evidence_quote: We conducted 60 trials on the Toyota HSR (20 per model) on a pick-up task... Each trial was graded on a 4-point rubric
statement: Real-robot validation was conducted using 60 trials on the Toyota HSR performing a pick-up task, with each trial graded on a 4-point rubric.

evidence_quote: We address this through: (1) a two-phase fine-tuning pipeline for SmolVLA with native 11D output
statement: The authors propose a two-phase fine-tuning pipeline for SmolVLA that natively supports 11D output.

evidence_quote: full fine-tuning exceeds 24 GB VRAM, and LoRA is incompatible with the architecture of the provided checkpoint.

evidence_quote: At the core of WLA lies an autoregressive (AR) Transformer backbone, instead of a bidirectional diffusion Transformer as in WAMs, to predict the next state, comprising the semantic-level textual intention and complementary fine-grained physical dynamics.
statement: The core of the WLA model is an autoregressive (AR) Transformer backbone that predicts the next state, comprising semantic-level textual intention and fine-grained physical dynamics.

evidence_quote: WLA leverages meta-queries to make the world prediction implicitly impact the action generation so that the former can be disabled during inference.
statement: WLA uses meta-queries to allow world prediction to implicitly impact action generation, enabling the world prediction to be disabled during inference.

evidence_quote: Evaluations across simulated and real-world environments demonstrate that WLA-0 achieves state-of-the-art multi-task and long-horizon learning abilities, e.g., 92.94% success rate on RoboTwin2.0 Clean and 56.5% success rate on RMBench.
statement: WLA-0 achieves a 92.94% success rate on the RoboTwin2.0 Clean benchmark and a 56.5% success rate on RMBench.

evidence_quote: WLA-0 also holds the promise to learn novel tasks directly from cross-embodiment robot videos without action annotations.

evidence_quote: our method surpasses the best baseline by approximately 14% on average performance scores.
statement: The proposed method outperforms the best baseline by an average of approximately 14% in performance scores.

evidence_quote: an action-information-bottleneck (action-IB) training objective that back-propagates the closed-loop action-chunk loss through the gate decision, directly aligning write selection with decision quality
statement: The AURA-Mem gate is trained using an action-information-bottleneck (action-IB) objective that back-propagates the closed-loop action-chunk loss through the gate decision.

evidence_quote: a training-time write-rate control ($\rho$, the target write rate, with $\gamma$ its penalty weight) that places the model anywhere on the write-bandwidth/accuracy frontier by selecting a target at train time

statement: The asynchronous chunk execution method is built on rectified flow action decoding, which uses noise-to-data interpolation from flow-based generative modeling.

evidence_quote: Simulation experiments use standard robot learning benchmarks such as LIBERO and related language-conditioned manipulation settings
statement: CT-VAM is evaluated on the LIBERO benchmark for simulation experiments to assess its visuomotor performance.

evidence_quote: Our extensive experiments on the AAPM dataset across multiple 3D CT reconstruction tasks demonstrate that...

evidence_quote: Furthermore, achieving data consistency in inverse problems typically requires injecting stochastic noise during the reverse refinement process, which invalidates the deterministic trajectory assumptions relied upon by unconditional scheduling algorithms, rendering them ineffective for complex conditional inverse solvers.
